h: Thyroid cancer with RET/PTC mutation: expected histology?
a: Psammoma bodies and empty-appearing (Orphan Annie) nuclei
p: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is the most common thyroid cancer, spreads via lymphatics, and has an excellent prognosis; RET/PTC rearrangements and BRAF are typical. Medullary carcinoma (calcitonin, amyloid) is RET-germline in MEN2.

h: Persistent hoarseness, hemoptysis, vegetating vocal cord lesion: diagnosis?
p: Hoarseness lasting weeks with a vocal cord mass in a smoker suggests squamous cell laryngeal cancer; direct laryngoscopy with biopsy is needed.

h: Child with cystic posterior fossa mass, corkscrew eosinophilic fibers: tumor?
p: Pilocytic astrocytoma: most common pediatric glioma, cerebellar, GFAP+, Rosenthal fibers, good prognosis after resection. Medulloblastoma is a solid, small-blue-cell midline tumor.

h: Antipsychotic-induced galactorrhea: which dopamine pathway is blocked?
p: Dopamine from the tuberoinfundibular tract normally inhibits prolactin; D2 blockade (risperidone) raises prolactin, causing galactorrhea and amenorrhea. Nigrostriatal blockade causes parkinsonism.

h: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperreflexia) unresponsive to benzodiazepine: antidote?
p: Cyproheptadine is a 5-HT2A antagonist used for serotonin syndrome (clonus, hyperreflexia, hyperthermia, diarrhea) alongside benzodiazepines and stopping the serotonergic drugs.

h: Helicase knocked out during DNA replication: what fails?
p: Helicase separates the parental strands at the fork; topoisomerase relieves supercoiling and primase makes the RNA primer.

h: Wet macular degeneration (wavy central vision): intravitreal drug mechanism?
p: Wet AMD is treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF agents (bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept). Corneal cross-linking treats keratoconus.

h: Left varicocele: impaired flow at which junction?
a: Left testicular vein into left renal vein
d: Left testicular artery off the aorta
p: The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein at a right angle, so flow is poorer; a new right-sided varicocele or non-reducing one should prompt a search for a retroperitoneal mass.

h: Blue fingers in the cold after a viral infection: Coombs result?
p: Cold agglutinin disease: IgM binds RBCs in the cold and fixes complement, so direct Coombs is C3-positive (IgG-negative); seen after Mycoplasma pneumoniae or EBV.

h: Sciatica with positive straight-leg raise after heavy lifting: cause?
p: Disc herniation compresses lumbosacral roots (L5/S1 most often), causing radicular pain below the knee; bilateral deficits with saddle numbness suggest cauda equina syndrome.

h: Most common cause of appendicitis in children?
p: In children obstruction is usually from lymphoid hyperplasia (often post-viral); in adults a fecalith is the commonest obstruction.

h: Chronic H. pylori gastritis: B-cell neoplasm risk?
p: H. pylori drives chronic antigenic stimulation; early low-grade MALT lymphoma may regress with eradication therapy. H. pylori also raises gastric adenocarcinoma risk.

h: Chest stab wound, muffled heart sounds, JVD, hypotension: expected sign?
p: Tamponade: inspiratory SBP drop above 10 mmHg. Tension pneumothorax has absent breath sounds and tracheal shift; flail chest shows paradoxical motion.

h: Which organelle makes steroid hormones and detoxifies drugs?
p: Smooth ER is abundant in steroid-producing cells (adrenal cortex, gonads) and hepatocytes (cytochrome P450); rough ER makes secretory proteins.

h: COPD: spirometry pattern?
a: Low FEV1/FVC with high total lung capacity
d: High FEV1/FVC with low total lung capacity
Normal FEV1/FVC with low total lung capacity
p: Obstructive disease reduces FEV1 more than FVC (ratio under 0.7) and air trapping raises TLC and RV; restrictive disease has a normal or high ratio with low TLC.

h: Fever and chills hours after transfusion: how to prevent?
d: ABO and Rh typing before transfusion
p: Febrile nonhemolytic reactions come from recipient antibodies against donor leukocytes and cytokines; leukoreduction and antipyretics prevent or treat them.

h: ARDS: which finding stays normal?
p: ARDS is noncardiogenic pulmonary edema: bilateral infiltrates, refractory hypoxemia and high A-a gradient with a normal pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.

h: Neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia unresponsive to phototherapy: diagnosis?
p: Type I has absent UDP-glucuronosyltransferase and needs exchange transfusion or liver transplant; type II responds to phenobarbital; Gilbert is mild and benign.

h: Substance to measure extracellular fluid volume?
p: Mannitol, inulin and sucrose distribute in ECF; Evans blue and labeled albumin measure plasma volume; heavy water measures total body water.

h: Th2 cytokine causing B cell class switching to IgE?
p: IL-4 and IL-13 drive IgE switching and Th2 differentiation; IL-5 drives IgA switching and eosinophils.

h: QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic with the lowest torsades risk?
p: Although amiodarone (class III) prolongs QT, torsades is uncommon; sotalol, ibutilide, quinidine and dofetilide carry high torsades risk.

h: Severe pain with defecation, bright red blood, sphincter spasm: diagnosis?
p: Anal fissures (usually posterior midline) cause tearing pain and bright red streaks; treat with fiber, sitz baths and topical nifedipine or nitroglycerin.

h: Rhizomelic short limbs, macrocephaly, normal intelligence: diagnosis?
p: FGFR3 gain-of-function (autosomal dominant, usually de novo from older fathers) impairs endochondral ossification; trunk normal, limbs short.
